full_judgment: 5. The defendant Nos. 1-4 contested the suit by presenting written statement taking the stand that Sadar Akanda was the rightful owner of the suit land. Sadar Akanda died leaving behind 4 sons namely Mahmud Ali, Akbar Ali, Nayebullah and Kabaj Ali and one daughter. During the lifetime of Sadar Akand, Nayebullah died leaving son Reazul. Kabaj Ali, thereafter, died leaving two sons Mayezuddin and Ayenuddin. Sadar Akanda, Reazuddin, Moizuddin and Ayenuddin had 8 annas, 4 annas, 2 annas and 2 annas share respectively in the suit CS Khatian No. 142. Further pleading is that the heirs of Sadar Akand and Reazuddin, Moizuddin and Ayenuddin used to enjoy their properties amicably. Akbor died leaving a son Efazuddin and the said Efazuddin transferred 0.85 acres of land by way of sale deed dated 20-3-1943 AD to Siberuddin, the predecessor-in-interest of the defendants. It is also pleaded that Mofizuddin transferred the share inherited by him from his mother to the plaintiff and Amejuzzin on 4-10-1984. The plaintiff and Amejuddin, also, transferred 0.52 acres of land in favour of the father of the defendant Nos. 1-4, Siberuddin by way of a deed of transfer. It is also averred that Mahmud Ali transferred 0.52 acres of land in favour of Siberuddin, the predecessor father of the defendant Nos. 1-4 by way of sale deed dated 11-5-1957. It is further stated that the suitland had been correctly recorded in the name of Siberuddin, the predecessor father of the defendants. It is asserted that plaintiff had no possession on the suit land and, as such, the question of dispossession did not at all arise.
